newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Regional capital captured by Somali faction, reports.
newsitem.headline: Regional capital captured by Somali faction, reports.

text.p: Fighters of the Rahanwein Resistance Army captured regional capital Hoddur, 300 km (200 miles) northwest of Mogadishu, from the militia of Somali warlord Hussein Mohamed Aideed, radio reports from the area said on Sunday.
RRA military commanders were quoted as saying at least 25 Aideed fighters were killed and 58 wounded in several hours of fighting on Saturday. They gave no details of RRA casualties.
Other reports from the area said the casualty toll was much higher.

The Aideed faction made no comment on the reported fighting. But the Aideed militia, aided by reinforcements sent from Mogadishu, was reported to be re-grouping 50 km (30 miles) south of Hoddur with the aim of staging a counter-attack.
Somali leaders in Mogadishu expressed surprise at the fall of Hoddur to the RRA, who lost control of the town in January last year.
Residents of the area said tension had built up over collection of taxes in Hoddur by the Aideed faction. This had resulted in increased support for the RRA by local people.
The RRA is one of a number of armed factions controlling different areas in Somalia, which has not had an effective government since dictator Mohamed Siad Barre was ousted early in 1991.

The Aideed faction is the strongest in the country, controlling the southern sector of Mogadishu and a large area of central Somalia, but its claim to be the government of Somalia is not accepted by many of the rival groups.
